title: Tosefta Eruvin
text: Gentiles who come against Israelite towns - go forth to do battle against them carrying weapons, and they violate the prohibitions of the Sabbath on their account. When?  When they come to kill.  But if they do not come to kill, they do not go forth against them carrying weapons, and they do not violate the prohibitions of the Sabbath on their account. If they come against towns located near the frontier, even to grab straw, even to grab a loaf of bread, they go forth against them carrying weapons, and they violate the prohibitions of the Sabbath on their account. At first, they would leave their weapons in the house nearest the wall.  One time, they ran about and were in haste to grab their weapons, and they ended up killing one another.  They established that each one should go to one's house.

Five courtyards that open into an alleyway: It is prohibited to carry in and carry out from a courtyard to an alleyway, and from an alleyway to a courtyard. Vessels that have spent the Sabbath in the courtyard are permitted to carry within a courtyard, [but] those that are in an alleyway are prohibited. Rabbi Shimon permits it, and so too would Rabbi Shimon say, it is permitted to carry in and carry out from an alleyway to a courtyard and from a courtyard to a roof, and from a roof to an enclosure (karpef), for anytime that [the residents of a courtyard] forgot to establish an eiruv, all of these [are considered to be] a single domain. Said Rebbi: When I was studying Torah at the place of Rabbi Shimon in Tekoa, we would carry oil in a towel from the courtyard to the roof, and from the roof to an enclosure, and from that enclosure to another enclosure, until we arrived to the spring, and we would bathe there. Said Rabbi [Yehuda], it so happened during a time of danger (i.e., Roman persecution), that we would carry up a Torah scroll from the courtyard to the roof, and from that roof to another roof, and we would read from it [there]. They said to him, a time of danger is no proof.
